theory Bags

Multisets (Bags)

Bags as quotient types over lists by permutation, representative independence, and algebraic laws.

Constable et al. §10.3

Multisets (Bags) as an abstract data type via quotients in CTT.

This theory formalizes: 1. Multiplicity counting of elements in a list (`Count`). 2. Permutation equivalence (`PermEq`): lists with the same counts for every atom. 3. The multiset quotient type `Bag == (List Atom) // PermEq`. 4. Proof that `PermEq` is an equivalence relation (reflexive, symmetric, transitive). 5. Formation of the `Bag` type in universe `U{i}`. 6. Bag operations: `BEmpty`, `BSingleton`, `BAdd`, `BUnion`. 7. Representation independence and algebraic union laws on the quotient.

18 theorems, 8 abstractions, checked by replaying their tactic scripts on the kernel. Hover any piece of syntax for its kind, surface form, and uniform term; open Tactics, Proof, or Analysis to go deeper.

Original source file
-- | Multisets (Bags) as an abstract data type via quotients in CTT.
--
-- This theory formalizes:
-- 1. Multiplicity counting of elements in a list (`Count`).
-- 2. Permutation equivalence (`PermEq`): lists with the same counts for every atom.
-- 3. The multiset quotient type `Bag == (List Atom) // PermEq`.
-- 4. Proof that `PermEq` is an equivalence relation (reflexive, symmetric, transitive).
-- 5. Formation of the `Bag` type in universe `U{i}`.
-- 6. Bag operations: `BEmpty`, `BSingleton`, `BAdd`, `BUnion`.
-- 7. Representation independence and algebraic union laws on the quotient.
theory Bags

comment book "Multisets (Bags) as an abstract data type via quotient types."

abs Append(xs; ys) == list_ind xs (ys) (h, t, ih. h :: ih)

abs Count(x; l) ==
  list_ind l 0 (h, t, ih. atom_eq h x (ih + 1) ih)

abs PermEq(l1; l2) ==
  ∀x:Atom. Count(x; l1) = Count(x; l2) ∈ Int

abs Bag == (l1, l2):(List Atom) // PermEq(l1; l2)

abs BEmpty == []
abs BSingleton(x) == x :: []
abs BAdd(x; b) == x :: b
abs BUnion(b1; b2) == Append(b1; b2)

soft Append, Count, PermEq, Bag, BEmpty, BSingleton, BAdd, BUnion

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Count reduction equations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem count_nil :
  ∀x:Atom. Count(x; []) = 0 ∈ Int
proof
  intro x
  reduce
  eq THEN auto
qed

theorem count_hit :
  Count("x"; "x" :: []) = 1 ∈ Int
proof
  reduce
  eq THEN auto
qed

theorem count_miss :
  Count("x"; "y" :: []) = 0 ∈ Int
proof
  reduce
  eq THEN auto
qed

theorem count_hit_step :
  ∀b:List Atom. Count("x"; "x" :: b) = Count("x"; b) + 1 ∈ Int
proof
  intro b
  reduce
  eq THEN auto
qed

theorem count_miss_step :
  ∀b:List Atom. Count("x"; "y" :: b) = Count("x"; b) ∈ Int
proof
  intro b
  reduce
  eq THEN auto
qed

-- Count queries evaluate identically regardless of insertion order:
theorem count_swap_hit_x :
  Count("x"; "x" :: "y" :: []) = Count("x"; "y" :: "x" :: []) ∈ Int
proof
  reduce
  eq THEN auto
qed

theorem count_swap_hit_y :
  Count("y"; "x" :: "y" :: []) = Count("y"; "y" :: "x" :: []) ∈ Int
proof
  reduce
  eq THEN auto
qed

theorem count_swap_miss_z :
  Count("z"; "x" :: "y" :: []) = Count("z"; "y" :: "x" :: []) ∈ Int
proof
  reduce
  eq THEN auto
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- PermEq is an equivalence relation
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem permeq_refl :
  ∀l:List Atom. PermEq(l; l)
proof
  intro l
  intro x
  eq THEN auto
qed

theorem permeq_sym :
  ∀l1:List Atom. ∀l2:List Atom.
    PermEq(l1; l2) → PermEq(l2; l1)
proof
  intro l1
  intro l2
  intro h
  intro x
  elim 3 with x THENL [
    hyp,
    elim 5
    eq
  ]
qed

theorem permeq_trans :
  ∀l1:List Atom. ∀l2:List Atom. ∀l3:List Atom.
    PermEq(l1; l2) → PermEq(l2; l3) → PermEq(l1; l3)
proof
  intro l1
  intro l2
  intro l3
  intro h12
  intro h23
  intro x
  elim 4 with x THENL [
    hyp,
    elim 5 with x THENL [
      hyp,
      elim 7 THEN hyp
    ]
  ]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Formation: Bag is a type
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem bag_type :
  Bag ∈ U{i}
proof
  eq THENL [
    eq,
    eq,
    intro z THEN eq THEN auto,
    lemma permeq_sym [x, y] THEN elim 4 with p THENL [hyp, hyp],
    lemma permeq_trans [x, y, z] THEN elim 6 with p THENL [hyp, elim 7 with q THENL [hyp, hyp]]
  ]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Representatives and quotient membership
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem list_to_bag :
  ∀l:List Atom. l ∈ Bag
proof
  intro l
  eq THENL [
    hyp,
    hyp,
    lemma permeq_refl [l] THEN hyp
  ]
qed

theorem bempty_in_bag :
  BEmpty ∈ Bag
proof
  eq THENL [
    eq,
    eq,
    lemma permeq_refl [[]] THEN hyp
  ]
qed

theorem bsingleton_in_bag :
  ∀x:Atom. BSingleton(x) ∈ Bag
proof
  intro x
  eq THENL [
    auto,
    auto,
    lemma permeq_refl [x :: []] THEN hyp
  ]
qed

theorem badd_in_bag :
  ∀x:Atom. ∀b:List Atom. BAdd(x; b) ∈ Bag
proof
  intro x
  intro b
  eq THENL [
    auto,
    auto,
    lemma permeq_refl [x :: b] THEN hyp
  ]
qed

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Union identity laws on the quotient
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theorem bunion_nil_l :
  ∀b:List Atom. BUnion([]; b) = b ∈ Bag
proof
  intro b
  reduce
  eq THENL [
    hyp,
    hyp,
    lemma permeq_refl [b] THEN hyp
  ]
qed

theorem bunion_cons_l :
  ∀x:Atom. ∀xs:List Atom. ∀ys:List Atom.
    BUnion(x :: xs; ys) = BAdd(x; BUnion(xs; ys)) ∈ Bag
proof
  intro x
  intro xs
  intro ys
  reduce
  eq THENL [
    auto,
    auto,
    lemma permeq_refl [x :: Append(xs; ys)] THEN hyp
  ]
qed
